12	# Spacetime Canvas — Implementation Plan
13	
14	**Feature family:** Temporal Observatory
15	**This document:** the build plan for the **Spacetime Canvas** — the first and
16	load-bearing surface of the family.
17	**Ticket:** T-047 (Foundation) → this plan expands it.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 0. Why "Spacetime Canvas"
22	
23	The platform already has a **Research Canvas**: a surface where the user
24	arranges *ideas* — entities, relationships, notes — in conceptual space.
25	
26	The **Spacetime Canvas** is its sibling: the same verb, a different axis. The
27	user arranges and traverses *evidence in space and time*. Same posture
28	(a canvas you work on, not a chart you look at), same design grammar,
29	orthogonal dimension.
30	
31	This naming is deliberate and load-bearing. Keep the pairing visible in
32	routes, module names, and copy:
33	
34	| Surface | Organizes | Route | Module |
35	|---|---|---|---|
36	| Research Canvas | ideas, entities, relations | `/research-canvas` | `features/mindmap/` |
37	| Spacetime Canvas | evidence across space + time | `/spacetime` | `features/spacetime/` |
38	
39	---
40	
41	## 1. The architectural finding (load-bearing)
42	
43	The reference scroll UI — `v0-ultraterrestrial-research-canva.vercel.app/timeline-explorer`
44	— was inspected live on 2026-08-01. What it actually is:
45	
46	```
47	Next.js  +  GSAP  +  Lenis (smooth scroll)
48	22,056px scroll height  ≈  24 viewport-heights,  19 encounters
49	ZERO <canvas> elements.  No Three.js, no R3F, no WebGL.
50	```
51	
52	Its DOM has exactly two structural layers:
53	
54	```
55	.fixed.inset-0.overflow-hidden.bg-neutral-950     ← BACKGROUND: a stack of 8
56	   ├── img roswell-ufo-crash-site-desert.jpg         cross-fading <img> era
57	   ├── img washington-dc-capitol-ufo-1952.jpg        plates, pinned to viewport
58	   ├── img socorro-new-mexico-ufo-egg-shaped…
59	   └── …
60	
61	.absolute.inset-0                                  ← NARRATIVE: CSS 3D
62	   perspective: 900px                                 cards fly toward the
63	   transform-style: preserve-3d                       viewer on scroll
64	   └── matrix3d(…, translateZ(-674px), …)
65	```
66	
67	**The seam:** the background is a *slot*, currently filled with static images,
68	and the narrative layer above it never touches WebGL. So:
69	
70	> **The Spacetime Canvas globe drops into the `.fixed.inset-0` slot, and the
71	> scroll narrative becomes Guided Investigations rendered as descent.**
72	
73	This unifies three storyboarded concepts into one surface instead of three:
74	
75	- **Concept 01 (Spacetime Canvas)** → the fixed globe layer
76	- **Concept 02 (Guided Investigation)** → the scrolling waypoint cards
77	- The **adaptive temporal dial** → the left rail, already present as a year ladder
78	
79	Scroll position becomes the single driver: `scrollProgress → temporalCursor →
80	{ globe camera, active layers, visible waypoint }`.
81	
82	### Why this is worth doing rather than building two surfaces
83	
84	The alternative — a globe page and a separate scroll page — reproduces exactly
85	the failure ADR 0002 rejected for GL4SS: two navigation systems, two state
86	models, a jarring seam between "exploring" and "reading." One surface with a
87	live background is the whole point.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## 2. Three risks to verify *while* building
92	
93	These are not blockers; they are measurements to take at the point they become
94	answerable. Do not hand-wave any of them.
95	
96	### R1 — `position: fixed` WebGL under a `preserve-3d` sibling
97	
98	An `<img>` stack is nearly free to keep pinned. A live deck.gl globe re-renders
99	every frame *while* Lenis drives `matrix3d` transforms on the sibling layer.
100	Compositing a `preserve-3d` subtree over a continuously-repainting WebGL canv...

## 2. WHERE DATA ACTUALLY LANDS

**Verdict: NOT the same Neon Postgres the Next.js app reads, for the live path.** The canonical write path (`main.py` → `lib/knowledge_base_service.py` → `lib/knowledge_base_crud.py`) writes to:
1. **Filesystem**: `packages/knowledge-base/sources/{files,transcripts,web}/` + `packages/knowledge-base/metadata/index.json` — this directory IS shared with the rest of the monorepo (matches CLAUDE.md's note that `case_files` → `files` rename), but it's a flat-file JSON index, not Postgres.
2. **Upstash Search** (`IntegratedUpstashSyncer`) — a separate hosted vector index, opaque embedding model (Upstash Search auto-embeds server-side; no model/dimension is ever specified in `lib/sync_to_upstash_search_integrated.py` or `lib/upstash/vector.py` — zero hits for "model"/"embed"/"dimension" in either file).
3. **OpenAI vector store** via `--upload` — this genuinely is shared infrastructure with the Next.js mindmap agent (same `file_search` vector store family per CLAUDE.md).

A real shared-Postgres client (`lib/db/postgres_client.py`) exists, correctly designed to resolve `packages/db/.env`'s `DATABASE_URL` as a fallback (`lib/db/postgres_client.py:29-31,64-74`) — but it is **not called by anything except its own test**. So the "completely disconnected" claim in CLAUDE.md is *currently accurate for the live ingestion path*, but a bridge has been half-built (issue #154) and not finished/wired in.

**Schema actually written by Python side**: no formal SQL schema — `Document` dataclass (`lib/knowledge_base_crud.py:20-29`: `id, title, content, source, doc_type, created_at, updated_at, metadata, tags`) serialized to per-document `metadata.json` + a flat `index.json` dict keyed by `doc_id`.

## 3. EMBEDDING COMPATIBILITY VERDICT

**Fragmented, not matching the locked model, in the paths that use local embeddings at all:**
- Live ingestion path (Upstash Search): embedding model is **opaque/Upstash-managed**, never specified in code — cannot be verified as 1536-dim `text-embedding-3-small`, and Upstash Search's own embedding models are not OpenAI's.
- `lib/storage/pgvector_library.py:66,79`: hardcoded default `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, **384 dims** — directly incompatible with the locked 1536-dim standard, though this module is orphaned/unused.
- `lib/connectors/ultraterrestrial_db.py:75,140`: same 384-dim default, OpenAI 1536-dim only as a fallback, and this module is migration-script-only.
- Historical evidence of the mismatch being a known problem: `scripts/analyze_csv_structure.py:161-162` — `"⚠️ Found 1536D embeddings - need conversion to 384D"` — i.e., there was a prior migration attempting to convert 1536D vectors DOWN to 384D for compatibility with the local pgvector/CocoIndex path.
- Genuine 1536/`text-embedding-3-small` usage exists in `lib/openai_client/upload.py:105` (file upload to OpenAI, correct — that's OpenAI's own embedding, matches), `lib/knowledge_base.py:127,172`, and agent files (`agents/deep_knowledge.py:40`, `agents/entity_extraction_agent.py:614`) — but none of these write into the shared Neon `documents`/entity tables; they're OpenAI-native paths.

**Bottom line: none of the vectors the Python side actually produces today land in the locked 1536-dim Neon pgvector store. The one module that hardcodes a different model (384-dim) is unused; the live path's embedding model is not inspectable from static code (Upstash-managed).**

## 4. METADATA / PROVENANCE MODEL AS-BUILT

- **Content-hash ID scheme, real and consistently used**: `doc_id = hashlib.md5(content.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]` (`lib/knowledge_base_crud.py:83,141`) for articles; YouTube content uses `video_id` as `doc_id` directly (`lib/knowledge_base_service.py:93-94`). This is a genuine content-addressed ID — re-ingesting identical content is idempotent by construction; a single-character content change produces a new ID (no diffing/versioning).
- **No ingestion-run ID** anywhere in the CRUD/service layer — no batch/run identifier ties a set of documents to one ingestion invocation.
- **Lineage source→document is real but shallow**: `Document.source` field captures the origin URL/file path; there's no page-number or offset-level provenance (no chunk→page traceability) — the CRUD layer operates at whole-document granularity, not chunk granularity. Chunking (where it exists, in `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py`) is a separate, unwired subsystem (see §5).
- **`packages/knowledge-base/metadata/registry.jsonl` and `redirect.json` exist on disk but are both 0 bytes** — provisioned, never populated.

## 5. DOMAIN-VOCABULARY (CONTEXT.md) ENFORCEMENT VERDICT

**Mostly docs-only, with one real but unwired exception.** `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py:9` explicitly encodes the CONTEXT.md rule: `"Chunk bodies remain Evidence-only (ADR-0001): never embed agent Inference."` — this is genuine, deliberate enforcement of the Claim/Evidence/Inference distinction, referencing an actual ADR. **However, `rag_prompt_pipeline.py` is not called by `main.py` or any live entrypoint** — its only referrers are its own package `__init__.py` (a re-export, not a call) and `tests/test_rag_prompt_pipeline_wiring.py`. It's a built-but-not-integrated pipeline. The `Document` dataclass that IS live (`lib/knowledge_base_crud.py`) has no evidentiary-state field, no Claim/Inference/Evidence tagging at all.

## 6. CANONICAL-STORE DECISION SURFACE

Given what's actually working vs. what exists on paper:

**Most working code behind it**: Upstash Search (`IntegratedUpstashSyncer`) + local filesystem/JSON — this is the only pairing that is both imported by the live entrypoint (`main.py`) AND has a non-empty, recently-updated data store (564 docs, updated yesterday).

**Most data already in it**: same pairing — filesystem (833 transcripts + 68 web + 48 files on disk) and the JSON index. The shared Neon Postgres has the 126,483 records/6,540 vectors, but essentially none of that volume was produced by the Python disclosure-rag ingestion path — it's populated by `packages/db` rebuild scripts, a completely separate code path.

**Migration cost to make Neon pgvector canonical for Python-side ingestion**, given 6,540 existing vectors locked at 1536-dim:
- Cheapest technically: finish wiring `lib/db/postgres_client.py` (already correctly points at the shared endpoint) into `knowledge_base_service.py`'s write path, and swap `IntegratedUpstashSyncer` calls for direct `INSERT ... embedding` calls using `text-embedding-3-small`. The client-and-endpoint half of this bridge is already built (issue #154) — this is finishing a 60%-done PR, not new architecture.
- Requires: (a) re-embedding all 564 already-ingested documents with `text-embedding-3-small` since none of their current vectors (Upstash-managed, unknown model) are reusable; (b) deciding whether `packages/knowledge-base/` filesystem storage is retired or kept as the raw-content store with Postgres holding only chunks+embeddings+metadata (recommend keeping filesystem for raw source files, Postgres for the queryable/embedded layer — mirrors what `packages/db` already does for the rest of the platform).
- Discard-cost of the alternatives is near zero: pgvector_library.py, FAISS backends, ultraterrestrial_db.py, and the Xata-writing entity path are all either unused or targeting a retired backend already — nothing of value is lost by deleting them.

**Recommendation**: Neon pgvector via `lib/db/postgres_client.py`, using `text-embedding-3-small`/1536, is the only option that (a) matches the platform's locked embedding standard, (b) unifies with the 126,483-record/6,540-vector store the rest of the app already queries, and (c) has a half-finished, well-documented bridge already merged. Upstash Search should be deprecated once the bridge ships — it currently duplicates the vector-store role with an opaque embedding model that can never be queried by the Next.js FTS+pgvector path. The Xata-writing entity-extraction code (`entity_creator.py`) should be either deleted or repointed at `packages/db`'s Postgres entity tables — it is currently non-functional against a retired backend.

## 7. DOC-VS-REALITY CONTRADICTIONS

- `QUINUPLE_RAG_ARCHITECTURE_DOCUMENTATION.md` (dated Sept 1 2025, ~11 months stale relative to session date 2026-08-01) claims Xata is "✅ FULLY OPERATIONAL" with 230,998+ records and is Layer 2 of a 5-layer live architecture. CLAUDE.md (current, authoritative) says Xata is **retired** and the real count is 126,483 records in Neon Postgres. Both cannot be current; CLAUDE.md matches what `postgres_client.py`'s docstring and recent commit history describe, so the Quinuple doc is stale, not CLAUDE.md.
- Same doc's "Usage Example" (`lib/simple_unified_search.py`, `QuinupleRAGUnifiedSearch`) describes a system with zero real callers — pure documentation-driven-development that was never wired up.
- `COMPREHENSIVE_RAG_DOCUMENTATION.md` similarly frames "Quinuple RAG Engine" as the core architecture (header line 12) without flagging that most of the 5 layers are orphaned modules.
- CLAUDE.md's own "Database Work" section (stale, as team-lead flagged) says "Update Xata schema through dashboard first / run `xata codegen`" — confirmed stale by this audit: the one place Xata is genuinely still called (`entity_creator.py:249`) is doing so against a retired backend, not because that guidance is being followed productively.
- `lib/unified_rag_orchestrator.py`'s docstring architecture diagram (Tier 1 OpenAI / Tier 2 local systems) references `TripleRAGSchemaAdapter`, whose source file has been deleted (only a stale `.pyc` remains) — the orchestrator's own stated architecture no longer matches what it can actually import.
- CLAUDE.md's "completely disconnected" claim about the Python RAG system is **accurate for the live write path today**, but incomplete context: a bridge (`lib/db/postgres_client.py`, issue #154) already exists and correctly targets the shared endpoint — it's just not called yet. Worth noting as "not yet contradicted, but about to become stale" if issue #154 continues.

All findings above are grounded in call-graph verification (who actually imports/calls whom), not just presence of a file or a docstring's claim.

## 4. B↔C GAPS — VERDICT: NO SINGLE RELIABLE JOIN KEY EXISTS

index.json is keyed by 12-hex doc-ids tied to `original_path` (a disk path). Postgres `documents` is keyed by `doc_*` ids with a `metadata` jsonb containing only `{path, date, yt_id, filename, slug}` — **no field references index.json's doc ids or its path convention.** Raw count comparison (564 vs 189) is meaningless without a join; many Postgres `documents` rows are LLM-authored analyses ("Document Analysis:", "Research Agent Analysis:...") layered on top of source content, not 1:1 ingests of archive files.

Two indirect joins DO work, at high confidence:
- **yt_id**: 82 distinct non-"unknown" yt_ids in Postgres (137 transcript-source-type rows total → ~1.67 rows/video). **100% of Postgres yt_ids (82/82) resolve to a real disk folder.**
- **filename**: 20 distinct filenames on Postgres `pdf`-source-type rows. **100% (20/20) resolve to a real disk file.**
- **No usable join field for web/article content.** Disk-side: only 8 of 68 web files have a `metadata.json` sidecar, yielding just 6 distinct extractable URLs. Postgres has 32 `source_type='web'` documents. Can't produce a real match/no-match count — this is the one leg of the archive with no reliable reconciliation path at all, not an estimate I'm willing to make up.
- `document_chunks` orphan check: **0 orphans** — every chunk's `document` FK resolves to a real `documents.id`.
- Stale-naming leftover found: one Postgres PDF record's `metadata->>'filename'` literally reads `case_filesCrop Circles- "Signs" From Above or Human Artifacts?.pdf` — the pre-rename `case_files` prefix concatenated directly onto the filename (no separator), a dead reference from before the `case_files`→`files` rename that matches nothing on disk today.

## Interim findings

**The Python RAG system does not write to Neon.** The live path is `main.py` → `knowledge_base_service.py` → `knowledge_base_crud.py`, landing in three places: the filesystem, `metadata/index.json`, and **Upstash Search**. CLAUDE.md's "completely disconnected" claim is accurate — but a bridge (`lib/db/postgres_client.py`, issue #154) is already built, correctly pointed at the shared Neon endpoint, and called by *nothing but its own test*. That's a 60%-finished PR, not new architecture.

**The embedding standard is not actually held on the Python side.** Upstash Search auto-embeds server-side with an opaque model — no model or dimension is specified anywhere in that code path. So none of the vectors the Python pipeline produces today are compatible with the locked 1536-dim store. Two orphaned modules hardcode 384-dim `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, and there's fossil evidence of a past migration converting 1536D *down* to 384D.

**There is no reliable join key between the archive and the database.** `index.json` is keyed by 12-hex content-hash IDs tied to disk paths; Postgres `documents.metadata` carries only `{path, date, yt_id, filename, slug}` and references neither. Two indirect joins work at 100% (`yt_id`: 82/82, `filename`: 20/20), but **web/article content has no reconciliation path at all** — 32 web documents in Postgres, and only 6 extractable URLs on disk. This is the single most important structural finding.

**Verified numbers**, run against live Neon:

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| 30 tables / 126,483 records | Confirmed exact |
| 4,946 chunks / 6,540 vectors, all 1536-dim | Confirmed exact |
| "1,594 entity rows embedded" | **Wrong — actually 1,405**, across six tables |
| Orphaned chunks | 0 |
| `document_entities` table | Exists, **completely empty**, no embedding column |

**Archive state:** 946 real files, 564 index records, **390 files with no index entry** — though 298 of those are `graphify-out/` tool droppings, not source material. 94 byte-identical duplicate groups (3.0 MB). Roughly **52% of the archive has actually been ingested** (65% of PDFs, 91% of transcript folders).

Two traps worth naming now: `eisenhower_briefing (1).pdf` is a genuinely *different* document from its base file despite the `(1)` suffix — a naive dedup would destroy it. And one Postgres record still carries the mangled `case_filesCrop Circles-…pdf` filename from the rename, matching nothing on disk.

**One good surprise:** `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py` already encodes the ADR-0001 rule — chunk bodies stay Evidence-only, never embed agent Inference. It's real, deliberate, and completely unwired.

---

On the three decisions I was about to ask about — you interrupted, so I'll put my recommendations in the plan as named decisions with reasoning, and you can override any of them there rather than answering questions cold. My leanings, given the evidence: **Neon pgvector as the single store** (finishes an existing bridge, matches the locked model, and Upstash's opaque embeddings can never be queried by the app's FTS+vector path), **filesystem-as-truth with Postgres as a rebuildable derived index** (the archive is the thing that must survive), and **content-hash dedup plus resumable runs** (the hash scheme already exists at `knowledge_base_crud.py:83` — it just needs to reach the database).

I'll hold until the remaining three reports land, then write the plan to `docs/plans/2026-08-01-ingestion-hardening.md` with a T-048 ticket and a FEATURES.md entry.

Both lanes are officiated and the audit is complete. Here's where we're at.

## The two worklanes (now in `docs/plans/TODO.md`)

**Lane A — Corpus & Ingestion.** Owns `apps/disclosure-rag/`, `packages/knowledge-base/`, `packages/db/scripts/rebuild/`. Asks: *is the evidence correct, complete, traceable, durable?* Roadmap H0→H5. Active: **T-048**. Backlog: T-045.

**Lane B — Platform & Experience.** Owns `apps/app/`, `packages/ai/`, the canvases and agent paths. Asks: *can a researcher see, traverse, and reason about the evidence?* Roadmap M0→M4. Active: **T-047** (Spacetime Canvas).

**The one cross-lane dependency:** Lane B's M1 "Evidence instrument" — credibility filtering, source-cited inspection — cannot be built until Lane A ships H4. There is no provenance on 99% of archive records. Lane B's M0 is independent and can run in parallel.

## What the five audits found

Four things are structurally broken, and each is load-bearing for the next.

**Duplication is not a risk — it already happened.** 54 of 189 documents (28.6%) share a duplicate URL. `documents.id` hashes a *path*, not content, so the same video scraped into a different date folder gets a different id and `ON CONFLICT (id)` never fires. There's no content-hash column anywhere and no unique constraint on `url`.

**The archive silently destroys history.** Re-ingesting identical content on a *different calendar day* produces the same `doc_id` but a new date-stamped directory — the index entry is overwritten and the previous directory's files are orphaned forever, with no warning. Same-day re-ingest happens to work, accidentally. There's no file locking anywhere in the tree, so concurrent runs lose updates on `index.json`.

**4,946 embedded chunks are invisible to the product.** `document_chunks` isn't in `search.ts`'s or `related.ts`'s table lists. The entire chunk-level embedding investment is unreachable by `searchDatabase`, `searchAll`, or `getRelatedRecords` — its only consumer repo-wide is the ingest script's write path. Meanwhile two rogue `vectorize.ts` files exist in the app: one comments *"until document_chunks table is created"*, unaware it exists with 4,946 rows; the other targets a **Supabase** schema that isn't in Neon at all.

**No ANN index exists on any of the 10 vector columns.** Every similarity query sequential-scans. The schema knows — `0001_init.sql:22-26` says indexes go in migration 0002, and **0002 was never written**.

Plus: the archive is 36.6% `graphify-out/` tool cache (47 of which got ingested as documents); no hash is persisted despite one being computed and thrown away at `knowledge_base_crud.py:83`; `source_tier` is 100% NULL; and ADR-0001 has **unresolved merge-conflict markers committed into it**.

Two corrections worth noting: the documented "1,594 entity rows embedded" is actually **1,405**, and the `case_files` rename damage turned out to be trivial — one file, one path — not the systemic problem it looked like.

## What I'd do first

**H0 + H0.5, this week.** H0 stops new damage (dedup guard, atomic index writes, purge the tool cache, a `UNIQUE(url)` stopgap that would have caught all 54 duplicates). H0.5 is nearly free and high-payoff: add `document_chunks` to the search tables and write migration 0002 with HNSW indexes — that alone turns 4,946 already-paid-for embeddings from invisible into queryable.

Then H1 (content-hash identity) is the keystone everything else hangs on.

Plan is at `docs/plans/2026-08-01-ingestion-hardening.md`; T-048 and the lane taxonomy are in `docs/plans/TODO.md`. Nothing is committed yet — say the word and I'll commit, or start on H0.

One flag: I did **not** touch the 982-file index. It's still uncommitted, and the audits ran against the worktree on your "by design" answer.

_**Agent (2026-08-16 07:27:49Z)**_

Plan updated to your topology. What changed and why it matters:

**D1 and D2 are now settled**, marked as owner-specified rather than my recommendation. Both vector stores are retained as siblings under one AI Data Layer — Neon as system of record for structured retrieval, OpenAI for the Assistants `file_search` the mindmap agent uses. Upstash is out.

**Three consequences fall out of the fork that weren't in my linear version:**

The archive write can't depend on vectorization succeeding. That gives an intake ordering: **hash → archive → enqueue vectorization**. A failed OpenAI call or a Neon timeout must still leave a complete canonical record, because vectorization is retryable and lost source bytes are not.

The join key stops being something to reconstruct and becomes a property of the topology. One sha256 computed at the branch point, written into the archive record, `documents.content_hash`, and the OpenAI file attributes. Three sinks, one identity. This is what makes the web/article gap closeable — those 32 Postgres web documents have no join path today in *either* direction because nothing common was ever recorded; post-fork every item carries the same key regardless of source type.

Each branch reports to the same `ingestion_run` row, so a manifest can say *archived yes / embedded no / file_search yes* per item. That's the retry surface, and it's the thing that makes a dumped batch safe to re-run.

**Still open:** D3 (content-hash dedup + resumable runs) and D4 (`sources/` as immutable intake) remain my recommendations — though D4 is now implied by your diagram, since the archive branch being canonical is hard to reconcile with tool cache living inside it.

Nothing committed yet. Want me to commit the plan and TODO changes, or start on H0?

---

## On the boundary question

Neither of your two options is quite right, and the reason is that they both split by *package* when the real seam is **lifecycle**. Three zones:

**Ephemeral** — `disclosure-rag/.work/`, gitignored, nothing durable, safe to delete mid-run.
**Canonical** — `knowledge-base/sources/`, immutable, hash-manifested.
**Derived** — `knowledge-base/derived/`, regenerable: summaries, chunk sidecars, tool cache.

The invariant that makes it testable: **delete `disclosure-rag` entirely and lose zero data; delete `derived/` and regenerate it.**

Your Option A is close but puts unvalidated in-flight material inside the package whose entire claim is that everything in it is canonical. Option B is roughly today — and today's failure mode *is* durable material accumulating in a work area nobody treats as durable (that's how `data/playlist_ingestion/transcripts/` came to hold real source material).

Worth knowing: **your own `CORPUS.md` already proposed `derived/`.** The migration stopped at step one — `sources/` got renamed, `derived/` and `cases/` were never created, and `registry.jsonl` was left at 0 bytes. So this finishes an existing design rather than inventing a scheme.

## On the incoming intake

This changes the order of operations, and it's the most important thing I can tell you right now.

Dumped into the pipeline as it stands, a massive set would multiply the 54 duplicates, orphan a directory on every cross-day re-run, arrive with no hashes and no provenance, and risk re-contaminating `sources/` with tool output — at a scale where unwinding costs far more than preventing.

**Land H0 + H0.5 + H1 before the dump.** Dedup guard, atomic index writes, content-hash identity. Then the intake becomes the proving run for the hardened pipeline instead of the event that doubles the mess. It's also the last clean moment to fix identity before the corpus grows — every document that arrives unhashed is one you have to reconcile later without a join key.

I haven't written D5 into the plan or TODO yet — tell me if the three-zone split is right and I'll land it, or adjust if you'd rather keep intake staging inside `disclosure-rag` as a named durable zone.

process_urls() {
    local file=$1
    shift

    if [ -z "$file" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Error: URL file required${NC}"
        echo "Usage: $0 process-urls <FILE> [options]"
        exit 1
    fi

    if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}Error: File not found: $file${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi

    # main.py takes one input per invocation (no --url-file flag), so loop
    # over the file, skipping blank lines and # comments.
    echo -e "${BLUE}Processing URLs from: $file${NC}"
    local url
    while IFS= read -r url || [ -n "$url" ]; do
        url="${url%%#*}"
        url="$(echo "$url" | xargs)"
        [ -z "$url" ] && continue
        echo -e "${BLUE}--- $url${NC}"
        "$VENV_PYTHON" "$SCRIPT_DIR/main.py" "$url" "$@"
    done < "$file"
}

```python
def process_for_rag(
    self,
    content_text: str,
    *,
    provenance: str = "",
    filename_hint: str = "",
    content_type_override: Optional[str] = None,
    skip_ner: bool = False,
    run_ner: bool = True,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Run the registry-backed RAG/NER document pipeline. Returns structured
    classification, analysis, Evidence chunks, NER, and embeddable_texts
    suitable for vector indexing (Inference excluded)."""
    pipeline = RagPromptPipeline(run_ner=run_ner)
    return pipeline.process(
        content_text,
        provenance=provenance,
        filename_hint=filename_hint,
        content_type_override=content_type_override,
        skip_ner=skip_ner,
    ).to_dict()

def analyze_content_with_rag_pipeline(
    self,
    content_text: str,
    *,
    provenance: str = "",
    filename_hint: str = "",
    include_legacy_summary: bool = True,
    skip_ner: bool = False,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Legacy narrative summary + structured RAG pipeline artifact."""
    rag = self.process_for_rag(content_text, provenance=provenance,
                                filename_hint=filename_hint, skip_ner=skip_ner)
    legacy = self.analyze_content(content_text) if include_legacy_summary else None
    return {"legacy_analysis": legacy, "rag_pipeline": rag,
            "embeddable_texts": rag.get("embeddable_texts") or [], "status": rag.get("status")}
```

## 2. related.ts — NOT changed, and NOT adding document_chunks to its VECTOR_TABLES

Reasoning: related.ts's "similar" signal (`related.ts:39-42, 217-261`) exists to suggest canvas-addable *entities* — the seven tables in its `VECTOR_TABLES` are exactly the Research Canvas node types. document_chunks isn't a node type: there's no UI concept of adding "a chunk" to the canvas, `TITLE_EXPR`/`titleOf` (related.ts:44-62) have no chunk case (would silently fall back to raw `id`), and multiple chunks of the same source document would surface as several near-duplicate "similar" suggestions competing with — and diluting — the one genuinely useful signal, which is the parent `documents` row (already in scope). ## 3. Migration: packages/db/migrations/rebuild/0002_ann_indexes.sql (full file)

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- 0002_ann_indexes.sql  —  Vector ANN indexes + document_chunks integrity
-- Target: any managed Postgres 16+ with pgvector (Neon, current host). Host-portable.
-- Created: 2026-08-01
-- Why deferred from 0001: 0001_init.sql:22-26 explicitly reserved ANN index
-- creation for this migration, to run AFTER the embedding backfill (SP#2).
-- That backfill is now done — all 10 vector(1536) columns are either fully
-- populated or empty — so the indexes below can be created safely.
--
-- Conventions:
--   • HNSW, not IVFFlat — matches 0001's own stated reasoning: HNSW needs no
--     build-time data (unlike IVFFlat, whose list centroids are computed from
--     whatever rows exist at CREATE INDEX time) and handles incremental
--     inserts without a rebuild. Both properties matter here: mindmaps (0
--     rows) and summary_files (1 row, NULL embedding) are effectively empty
--     today but will grow.
--   • vector_cosine_ops — every cosine-similarity query in this codebase
--     (search.ts, related.ts) uses the <=> operator; the opclass must match.
--   • CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS — safe to re-run, and does not
--     hold a lock that blocks reads/writes on tables that already carry
--     production traffic (topics, key_figures, events, ..., document_chunks).
--
-- ⚠️  CRITICAL — DO NOT WRAP THIS FILE IN A TRANSACTION.
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block (Postgres
-- will reject it with "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a
-- transaction block"). Unlike 0001_init.sql, this file deliberately has NO
-- BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper. Apply it with a plain psql invocation, e.g.:
--     psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/rebuild/0002_ann_indexes.sql
-- \set ON_ERROR_STOP on below makes psql abort the whole file on the first
-- failing statement instead of printing an error and silently continuing —
-- without it, a failed ALTER TABLE (e.g. from the 0/4,946-nulls assumption
-- below going stale) would not stop the rest of the file from "succeeding".
-- Each CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statement commits its own catalog change as
-- it goes; if one is ever interrupted mid-build, check for an INVALID index
-- (`\d <table>` shows "INVALID") and DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY it before
-- re-running this file — re-running while it's INVALID will not repair it
-- because IF NOT EXISTS sees it as already there.
--
-- THIS MIGRATION HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED. It is authored for review; the lead
-- decides when/how it runs against the live database.
-- =============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP on

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- HNSW ANN indexes — one per vector(1536) column
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run first (before the document_chunks integrity fix below) because these
-- are the expensive, long-running part and carry no data risk — if the
-- integrity fix at the bottom ever needs to abort, the indexes should still
-- be left in place rather than lost to a whole-file failure.
--
-- All 10 are created, including the two effectively-empty tables (mindmaps,
-- summary_files). An HNSW build over 0 rows or all-NULL embeddings is
-- trivial and harmless — the index just starts empty and grows as rows are
-- inserted/backfilled, so there's no reason to special-case or skip them;
-- doing so would only mean remembering to add the index later.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_topics_embedding
    ON topics USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_key_figures_embedding
    ON key_figures USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_embedding
    ON events USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_organizations_embedding
    ON organizations USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_testimonies_embedding
    ON testimonies USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_documents_embedding
    ON documents USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_artifacts_embedding
    ON artifacts USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_chunks_embedding
    ON document_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Empty today (0 rows) — see comment above on why it's still created now.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_mindmaps_embedding
    ON mindmaps USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Empty today (1 row, NULL embedding) — see comment above on why it's still
-- created now.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_summary_files_embedding
    ON summary_files USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks: prevent partial-retry duplicates
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks currently has only a random-UUID PK (0001_init.sql:467-476)
-- and nothing stopping a partial ingest retry from re-inserting the same
-- (document, chunk_index) pair as a new row. scripts/rebuild/ingest.py always
-- supplies both values together on every INSERT (never NULL), so making them
-- NOT NULL matches how the table is actually written.
--
-- Verified 2026-08-01 against live data (read-only, before this file was
-- authored — re-run before applying if more ingestion has happened since):
--   SELECT document, chunk_index, COUNT(*) AS n
--   FROM document_chunks
--   WHERE document IS NOT NULL AND chunk_index IS NOT NULL
--   GROUP BY document, chunk_index HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
-- Result: 4,946/4,946 rows had non-NULL (document, chunk_index); 0 duplicate
-- groups; 0 rows with either column NULL.
--
-- Why NOT NULL first: a plain UNIQUE constraint in Postgres treats NULLs as
-- distinct from each other (NULLS DISTINCT is the default), so
-- UNIQUE(document, chunk_index) alone would NOT catch a retry that inserted
-- rows with a NULL in either column — it would silently let duplicates
-- through in exactly the failure mode this constraint exists to prevent.
-- Since live data already satisfies NOT NULL on both columns, enforcing it
-- closes that gap instead of leaving a documented loophole.
ALTER TABLE document_chunks ALTER COLUMN document SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE document_chunks ALTER COLUMN chunk_index SET NOT NULL;

-- Wrapped in a DO block per 0001_init.sql's own convention (see its
-- "FOREIGN KEY CONSTRAINTS" / "UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS" sections) so re-running
-- this file after a successful apply doesn't fail on duplicate_object.
DO $$ BEGIN
  ALTER TABLE document_chunks
    ADD CONSTRAINT uq_document_chunks_doc_index UNIQUE (document, chunk_index);
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;

-- =============================================================================
-- END 0002_ann_indexes.sql
-- =============================================================================
```

## Other notes worth your attention

- **Recall-shift in `vectorSearchAll`** (search.ts:246-261, unchanged code, new effect): it fans out across all `VECTOR_TABLES` splitting `limit` evenly per table. With document_chunks now included (4,946 rows) vs. 36–595 rows per entity table, chunk hits are likely to dominate the fused candidate pool in `searchDatabase`'s no-table-specified path. Not a bug, but a behavior shift worth watching — I didn't rebalance the allocation since that's a product decision, not a bug fix.
- `vectorSearch`'s `SELECT dc.*` still returns the raw `embedding` array in the JSON payload sent to the OpenAI tool output (`apps/app/.../mindmap/route.ts:456`), same as every other table today — pre-existing pattern, just flagging that chunk pools are bigger so the payload cost is now higher too.

Confirming again: **migration 0002 has not been run against the live database.** Only read-only SELECTs were executed. Nothing outside `packages/db/` was touched; nothing in `apps/disclosure-rag/` or `packages/knowledge-base/` was read or edited beyond one grep to confirm `ingest.py`'s insert pattern (read-only, for the NOT NULL justification above).

**H1** is the identity milestone in the hardening plan — the fix that makes everything else possible: persist a sha256 content hash on every archive record and add a matching column + unique constraint in Postgres, then re-key ingestion to dedup on that hash instead of on path. It's what closes the "54 duplicate documents" problem and the archive↔DB join-key gap. It comes right after H0/H0.5 (stop-the-bleeding + make chunks reachable) in the roadmap.

# Installation[¶](#installation "Link to this heading")

The VectorVFS package is available on PyPI. You can install it using pip (or any other package manager).

## Installing with pip[¶](#installing-with-pip "Link to this heading")

pip install vectorvfs

## Using the vfs Script[¶](#using-the-vfs-script "Link to this heading")

After installation, the `vfs` command-line tool is available:

vfs --help

# VectorVFS: Your Filesystem as a Vector Database[¶](#vectorvfs-your-filesystem-as-a-vector-database "Link to this heading")

VectorVFS is a lightweight Python package that transforms your Linux filesystem into a vector database by leveraging the native VFS (Virtual File System) extended attributes. Rather than maintaining a separate index or external database, VectorVFS stores vector embeddings directly alongside each file—turning your existing directory structure into an efficient and semantically searchable embedding store.

VectorVFS supports Meta’s Perception Encoders (PE) [\[arxiv\]](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13181) which includes image/video encoders for vision language understanding, it outperforms InternVL3, Qwen2.5VL and SigLIP2 for zero-shot image tasks. We support both CPU and GPU but if you have a large collection of images it might take a while in the first time to embed all items if you are not using a GPU.

Note

This is the first release of VectorVFS and we are expanding models and data types. Currently we support only Perception Encoders (PE) and images.

## Key Features[¶](#key-features "Link to this heading")

*   **Zero-overhead indexing** Embeddings are stored as extended attributes (xattrs) on each file, eliminating the need for external index files or services.
    
*   **Seamless retrieval** Perform searches across your filesystem, retrieving files by embedding similarity.
    
*   **Flexible embedding support** Plug in any embedding model—from pre-trained transformers to custom feature extractors—and let VectorVFS handle storage and lookup.
    
*   **Lightweight and portable** Built on native Linux VFS functionality, VectorVFS requires no additional daemons, background processes or databases.

_**Agent (2026-08-16 07:27:49Z)**_

**VectorVFS isn't a fit here, and I'd say so plainly rather than hedge.**

It stores embedding vectors as Linux ext4 **extended attributes (xattrs) on the files themselves** — no external index, no database, no daemon. Zero-overhead, philosophically close to D2's "filesystem is canonical." But three things rule it out for this pipeline:

1. **ext4-only, xattr-based.** Extended attributes don't survive git, most rsync/backup/object-storage transfers, or a cross-filesystem move — which directly undermines H5 (remote mirror) and the multi-machine reality of this repo (macOS dev, cloud storage). It would also mean *mutating* files in `sources/` to attach vectors, which conflicts with D5's write-once/immutable Inbound→Canonical model.
2. **Image-only, first release.** Currently supports exactly one embedding family — Meta's Perception Encoders, for images/video. The corpus here is overwhelmingly PDF/transcript/web text. Zero text-embedding support today, per their own docs ("currently we support only Perception Encoders and images").
3. **No ANN structure.** "No external index" sounds appealing until you remember the audit's own H0.5 finding — sequential-scan vector search was already a top hardening target. xattr storage has no HNSW equivalent; it doesn't solve that problem, it removes any lever to solve it.

Interesting idea, wrong tool for this job. Doesn't change D1/D2 — Neon pgvector stays canonical.

## Worklanes (officiated 2026-08-01)

All work belongs to exactly one lane. Every ticket carries a **Lane:** field. Plans,
roadmaps, and agent assignments are framed per lane; the three-tier system
(FEATURES → TODO → DAILY_WORK_PLAN) still applies *within* each lane.

### Lane A — Corpus & Ingestion

**Owns:** `apps/disclosure-rag/`, `packages/knowledge-base/`, `packages/db/scripts/rebuild/`
**Question it answers:** *is the evidence correct, complete, traceable, and durable?*
**Roadmap:** `docs/plans/2026-08-01-ingestion-hardening.md` (H0 → H5)
**Agents:** `disclosure-rag-agent`, `knowledge-base-agent`, `db-agent`

Lane A is upstream. Its output — a trustworthy, queryable, provenance-bearing corpus —
is the input Lane B renders. A defect here is invisible in the UI and corrupts every
surface downstream, which is why it gets its own lane rather than living as a backlog
tail behind product work.

### Lane B — Platform & Experience

**Owns:** `apps/app/`, `packages/ai/`, the research/spacetime canvases, agent chat paths
**Question it answers:** *can a researcher see, traverse, and reason about the evidence?*
**Roadmap:** `docs/plans/2026-08-01-spacetime-canvas-implementation.md` (M0 → M4)
**Agents:** `app-agent`, `research-ui-agent`

_**Agent (2026-08-16 07:27:49Z)**_

That fully explains it. The real mechanism wasn't an Artifact at all — it's a genuine Next.js route (`apps/app/src/app/design-lab/`) with real `.tsx` components, served by the dev server at `localhost:3000/design-lab`. Next.js Fast Refresh pushes file changes to the browser over a live socket connection — so when a previous session used Write/Edit on those files, your open tab updated **automatically**, no manual redeploy, no polling. That's genuinely real-time, using nothing but tools I already have plus infrastructure already in this repo.

That's the right mechanism for what you're asking. Building it that way — one condition: you need `bun run dev` running in `apps/app` with the page open in a tab, and updates will push live.

Key finds along the way:
- **RAG pipeline** (`process_for_rag`, `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py:35`) returns `status: ok|hold|rejected|error`. Old code printed ✅ unconditionally. Now only `ok` → ✅; `hold`/`rejected` → ⚠️; `error` → ❌ with `errors` list joined into detail.
